Educational Study Premise: Equities trading below declining 20-day and 60-day moving averages exhibit higher historical drawdown variance than cohorts that have reclaimed medium-term trend averages on expanding volume.

1. The Mathematics of Sub-MA60 Drawdowns

Investors often anchor to a company's prior 52-week peak. When an equity declines -35%, price alone can appear optically inexpensive even while earnings revisions and moving-average slopes remain negative.

2. Four Public Data Factors Tracked in Our Archive

Across our 26.8-year historical dataset (2000–2026), our educational factor score observes four public technical dimensions:

Factor 1 — 52-Week Drawdown Context: Measures distance from the trailing 52-week high to quantify prior valuation compression.

Factor 2 — Off-Low Stabilization: Measures distance above the trailing 52-week low to observe whether price has stopped recording lower lows.

Factor 3 — 20-Day & 60-Day Moving Average Alignment: Tracks whether daily closing price sits above or below medium-term trend averages.

Factor 4 — 10-Day Relative Volume Ratio: Compares 10-day average volume against trailing baseline volume on public tickers such as $CELH and $NVDA.

Frequently Asked Educational Questions

What public inputs are used in the TruthOfMarket factor score?

The educational factor score combines four public price-and-volume statistics: 52-week drawdown percentage, rebound distance from the 52-week low, position relative to 20-day and 60-day moving averages, and 10-day relative volume.

Does historical factor performance guarantee future returns?

No. All 2000–2026 empirical cohort statistics are historical mathematical observations for self-directed educational study and never guarantee future market outcomes.
